pages.heading: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors — definition and characteristic equation

blocks.text: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Let \(A\) be a square matrix of order \(n\). If there exists a non-zero column vector \(X\) and a scalar \(\lambda\) such that
\[AX=\lambda X,\]
\(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of the matrix \(A\).
\(X\) is an eigenvector of \(A\) corresponding to \(\lambda\).
Class example
\[A=\begin{bmatrix}5&4\\1&2\end{bmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}.\]
\[AX=\begin{bmatrix}24\\6\end{bmatrix}=6\begin{bmatrix}4\\1\end{bmatrix}=6X.\]
Hence \(\lambda=6\) is an eigenvalue and \(X=[4\;1]^T\) is a corresponding eigenvector.
The equation \(AX=\lambda X\) can be written as
\[(A-\lambda I)X=0.\]
This is a homogeneous system and has a non-trivial solution when
\[|A-\lambda I|=0.\]

This is the characteristic equation of the matrix. Its roots are called eigenvalues, characteristic roots or latent roots. For each eigenvalue \(\lambda\), the corresponding non-zero column vector \(X\) is called an eigenvector or characteristic vector of \(A\).

pages.heading: Properties of eigenvalues and eigenvectors — 1 to 6

blocks.text: 1. Eigenvalues of the inverse
If \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of a non-singular matrix \(A\), then \(1/\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A^{-1}\).
Proof: Given \(AX=\lambda X\),
\[X=\lambda A^{-1}X\quad\Rightarrow\quad A^{-1}X=\dfrac{1}{\lambda}X.\]
2. The eigenvalues of \(A\) and \(A^T\) are the same.
3. If \(\lambda\neq0\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\), then \(|A|/\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(\operatorname{adj}A\).
4. If \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\), then \(\lambda^m\) is an eigenvalue of \(A^m\).
5. If \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\), then \(a\lambda^2+b\lambda+c\) is an eigenvalue of \(aA^2+bA+cI\).
6. An eigenvector \(X\) of a matrix \(A\) cannot correspond to more than one eigenvalue of \(A\).

pages.heading: Further properties and a triangular-matrix example

blocks.text: 7. The sum of the eigenvalues of a matrix \(A\) is its trace, and the product of its eigenvalues is its determinant.
8. The eigenvalues of a triangular matrix or diagonal matrix are its diagonal elements.
9. If \(A\) and \(P\) are square matrices of the same order and \(P\) is non-singular, then \(A\) and \(P^{-1}AP\) have the same eigenvalues.
